Package bg.tu_varna.ks.models

Class Calendar

java.lang.Object
bg.tu_varna.ks.models.Calendar
public class Calendar extends Object
Central calendar model - holds all scheduled events from the currently opened file.

The class follows the Singleton pattern: there is always exactly one instance, accessible via getInstance(). This allows different commands to operate on a shared state without passing it explicitly between them.

In addition to storing the event collection, the calendar exposes business-logic operations: event validation, overlap detection, adding/removing events, holiday checks, and modifying individual fields of an event.

    • getInstance

      public static Calendar getInstance()

      If one does not yet exist, it is created lazily.

    • getEvents

      public List<Event> getEvents()
      Returns a direct reference to the list of events.

      Note: the list is mutable - direct operations on it will bypass the validations performed in addEvent(Event).

      Returns:
      the list of events

    • setEvents

      public void setEvents(List<Event> events)
      Sets a new list of events (used by JAXB during loading).

      If null is passed, a new empty list is stored instead, to avoid NullPointerException in the rest of the logic.

      Parameters:
      events - the new list of events; may be null

    • hasHoliday

      public boolean hasHoliday(LocalDate date)
      Checks whether the given date is marked as a holiday.

      A holiday means the date has an event whose name is "HOLIDAY" (case-insensitive).

      Parameters:
      date - the date to check
      Returns:
      true if the date is a holiday

    • setOption

      public boolean setOption(LocalDate date, LocalTime starttime, String option, String newValue)
      Modifies a single field of an existing event, identified by the date + start time pair.

      Supported field names are: "date", "starttime", "endtime", "name" and "note". If the modification leaves the event invalid or causes a conflict with another event, the change is rolled back and the original values are restored.

      Parameters:
      date - the date on which the event is scheduled
      starttime - the start time of the event
      option - the name of the field to be modified
      newValue - the new value as a string (parsed according to the target field)
      Returns:
      true on successful change; false if the option is unknown, the event is missing, or the change would produce an invalid/conflicting event
